name: method-latentloop-residual-muon
preserved: Middle half of physical layers is executed twice with every core owner shared (attention, router, experts, norms): the paper's MoE Loop (Section 2.1).

Every core attention/FFN residual branch is scaled by 0.25 in the first visit and by 1 in the second; independent prelude/coda use 1. (0.25, 1) is the paper's best fixed pair at 1.3B and 3B, below (1, 1) and (0.5, 0.5) (Section 3.1, Figure 2b).
Fixed depth, full BPTT, terminal cross entropy.
adaptations: This is LatentLoop Section 3.1's fixed (0.25, 1) per-visit residual finding on SMELT's loop, not the paper's final LatentLoop method. That method runs the first visit on a 2x mean-pooled sequence, writes it back through a learned scaled decoder and spends the saved compute on a wider model (Sections 3.2-3.4); it is not reproduced here because it needs sequence pooling, which the common model lacks.

Fixed (0.25, 1) instead of learned per-visit coefficients: the learned ones end near (0.27, 0.87) at 1.3B and (0.36, 1.09) at 3B, but the paper reports validation NLL only for fixed pairs (Section 3.1).
Attention stays shared across visits: at matched parameters, untying it in the full-resolution MoE Loop raised validation NLL from 2.0293 to 2.0319 (Table 5).

Track P2's Muon for hidden matrices (AdamW for embedding, head, routers, norms and other 1-D parameters), schedule and run settings replace the paper's training settings (AdamW, peak LR 1e-3 annealed to 1e-4 by 1-sqrt over the last 20%, 500 warmup updates, router aux 1e-3, FineWeb-Edu with the 32K TinyLlama tokenizer, 8 query and 2 KV heads with QK norm).
Publicly reconstructible DCLM replaces the original private corpus; the frozen manifest and tokenizer are separate comparison identities.
Common RMSNorm/RoPE/SwiGLU cells, softmax top-k with selected-weight normalization and dropless dispatch.

Track P2's Muon for hidden matrices (AdamW for embedding, head, routers, norms and other 1-D parameters) and independently owned input embedding/output head; no original-paper quality or scaling claim.

Geometry: M3's, unchanged, so this spec is LatentLoop Section 3.1's (0.25, 1) residual on M3: P2 SMELT's 12 physical layers as 3 prefix, 6 core layers run twice and 3 suffix (18 effective layers) at width 1056 (12 heads of 88), 88 experts of width 384, top-8, so LatentLoop-Residual - M3 differs only in the core residual scales, (0.25, 1) against SMELT's (0.5, 0.5), and parameters, training FLOPs and KV equal M3's; like the paper's MoE Loop against its Base (1184 against 1408 wide, 92 against 64 experts at 3B; Table 6), M3 is narrower than m0 with more experts (1056 against 1280, 88 against 64). M3 trains without activation checkpointing on 8 x H200 at local batch 16 (#180), and the residual scales change no activation, so neither does this.

Matrix initialization std=.02 and unit norm scales are P2's; seq 4096, 1,048,576 positions per update, the schedule (95-update linear warmup, constant peak, last 20% linear to 0) and the AdamW or Muon settings are Track P2's; the training recipe (objective, depth, aux coefficient, expert LR multiplier) is the constructor's.
